reason: Both correctly told her not to touch the plug or machine and to isolate at the consumer unit, but Conversation 1 handled the live emergency more decisively and calmly ('yes, go now', dry hands, main switch), then followed through with water isolation, controlled draining via the front filter, and a correct narrowing to the door seal after the filter and inlet checks came back dry, while honouring that she couldn't pull the machine out. Conversation 2 was safe but caused confusion by telling her not to cross the wet floor when she was already standing in it, never asked about the water supply or socket condition, repeated generic cause lists without any guided checks, and closed prematurely with a detergent tip rather than inspecting the seal or advising a seal replacement. Conversation 1 also gave electrician advice if the socket got wet and warned about an immediate trip; Conversation 2 escalated everything to an engineer without diagnosis.
